learning_objective: Show representative calibration inputs collecting activation extrema, then compare clipping under incomplete and representative ranges.
core_conclusion: Post-training calibration measures activation ranges using representative inputs; missing operating conditions can cause runtime clipping.

scenes.heading: Calibration observes activations
lines: Run representative inputs through the float model.
scenes.change: Examples enter one by one; resulting activations append to a collection and move the running maximum from0.4 to1 to2.
scenes.cause: Calibration measures activation ranges without updating learned weights.
scenes.result: The range encloses observed activations and the weights retain their initial values.
scenes.timing_reason: 4 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Range sets the quantization step
scenes.change: The observed endpoints anchor a quantized ruler and its interval size is computed from their span.
scenes.cause: The finite int8 code range must cover the selected real range.
scenes.result: A broader observed range produces a broader interval while preserving zero.
scenes.timing_reason: 4 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: A missing condition causes clipping
scenes.change: Identical runtime probes descend into both rulers; the narrow branch stops at1 whereas the representative branch reaches2.
scenes.cause: A narrow calibration set never observed the larger activation.
scenes.result: The missing-range branch loses half the value; the representative branch reaches its endpoint.
scenes.timing_reason: 5.5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3.5 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Coverage and precision both matter
lines: Wider range: less clipping, larger steps.
scenes.change: A0.7 probe snaps independently to both grids; enlarged ticks compare interval1/255 with2/255 while the earlier clipped high value stays as context.
scenes.cause: A fixed number of codes forces a coverage–resolution tradeoff.
scenes.result: The comparison separates range coverage from small rounding differences.
scenes.timing_reason: 5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

title: Calibration Dataset for Post-Training Quantization: Clipping
prompt:
Create a 31-second silent English animation of Calibration Dataset for Post-Training Quantization. At 0–7 s, feed representative inputs into a fixed float model and collect activations 0, 0.4, 1 and 2 without changing weights. At 7–14 s, map the observed 0–2 range onto 255 int8 intervals with scale 2/255. At 14–23 s, send the identical runtime value 2 into narrow 0–1 and representative 0–2 calibrations; show reconstructions 1 and 2. At 23–31 s, compare the two grid spacings and their reconstruction of 0.7, making the coverage–precision tradeoff visible.

Render a 1920×1080, 16:9 MP4 at 30 fps with no audio, using Helvetica Neue and line height 1.45. Use background layers #0e0e0e, #171b1c and #212629; input #56b4e9, operations #e69f00, results #009e73, clipping or rejection #d55e00, and secondary weights #cc79a7, with strong text #f8fafc and muted text #a8b4c4. Keep concise copy left and a large numerical SVG diagram right; fade and slide labels over 12–18 frames with 10-frame staggering, and bind moving marks, values and arithmetic to the same mechanism state.
